title: Residential Life mission and support
content:
## Mission

Residential Life aims to provide an inclusive, safe environment that supports learning and personal development, while improving services for students and guests.

## Guiding principles

- **Live:** Support safety, comfort, belonging, healthy relationships, empathy, respect, and freedom of thought and expression.
- **Learn:** Connect residential life with intellectual and personal growth; encourage collaboration, faculty relationships, and discussion of diversity and social justice.
- **Lead:** Encourage student participation, responsible citizenship, intentional community design, creative support for student success, and regular evaluation of housing practices.

## Finding people

The original directory contains the leadership team and faculty partners. Use it for current names, roles, and community assignments; this public collection does not replicate personal contact details or staff profiles.

title: RA role and communication standards
content:
## Daily communication

- Review university email and Microsoft Teams at least daily.
- Aim to answer messages and requests within 24 hours on business days.
- Use Teams for resident communication when suitable; use email or in-person follow-up when a matter is more formal or confidential.

## Professional boundaries

Keep communication respectful, inclusive, and professional. Protect confidential student information and internal Residential Life matters. Refer uncertain or sensitive communications to the supervising Residential Community Director (RCD), and promptly report concerns through the established channels.

## Media inquiries

The source says RAs should not represent Residential Life or the university in media statements, including student publications and online outlets. Direct inquiries to the Residential Life Center and notify the supervisor.

## Other role materials

The page identifies job descriptions, expectations, work agreements, evaluation materials, and accountability information as its scope. Those underlying documents have not been transcribed here; consult the source for them.

title: Bulletin boards and door decorations
content:
## Working with supplied boards

The source instructs RAs to keep the content of supplied bulletin boards intact and consult their supervisor about permitted theme changes and visual expectations.

## Rubric summary

The rubric uses four performance levels: Unsatisfactory, Needs Improvement, Meets Expectations, and Exceeds Expectations.

| Criterion | Meets Expectations | Exceeds Expectations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Appearance and theme | Coherent, organized layout; backing and borders; tape concealed; mostly clean edges | Creative, polished theme and consistently clean construction |
| Visual appeal | Presentation attracts the reader's attention | Includes a distinctive visual or three-dimensional feature |
| Legibility and space | Readable typed or die-cut information; some space may remain underused | Creative, readable presentation that makes fuller use of the board |
| CEM anchor alignment | Content connects clearly to a CEM anchor | Connection is purposeful, thorough, and impactful |
| Information depth | Informative content with some depth | Substantive material that serves readers with different prior knowledge |
| Interaction | Clear, engaging interactive component | Innovative and especially engaging interaction |
| Spelling and grammar | Few or no errors | Error-free work with close attention to detail |

The lower levels identify missing or inconsistent themes, weak presentation, hard-to-read text, poor spacing, incomplete anchor alignment, shallow information, weak or absent interaction, and language errors. Consult the original rubric for the precise evaluation language.

## Supporting resources

The source links to a bulletin-board photo upload destination, Fall Welcome Board, Campus Partner Bulletin Board Resources, Winter Transition Board, and Spring Closing Board. Shared access links are routed through the source page in this public repository.

title: Branding and departmental social media
content:
## Departmental account expectations

The source treats community social media accounts as university representation. It says university names, logos, trademarks, images, and campus-building imagery must not imply political or commercial institutional endorsement. It also restricts posts or reposts expressing an explicit or implicit endorsement or opinion.

## Handling negative feedback

The page instructs RAs to capture a screenshot and refer negative feedback to their RCD rather than responding themselves. It says not to delete posts without explicit direction from an RCD or Associate Director (AD).

## Brand resources

The page links to a WashU logo for program flyers, official logo usage guidance, and university brand guides. Use the official guidance and current approved assets.

title: Seasonal meeting agendas
content:
## Fall arrival and opening

| Meeting | When | Responsibility and purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move-in community meeting | Both first-year move-in nights; possibly transfer arrival night | RAs introduce themselves and explain immediate facilities and policy information |
| Residential community meeting | Sunday morning following first-year move-in | RCD leads, assisted by RAs and faculty; welcomes first-year residents and covers community information |
| Opening and community standards | First Monday of fall classes | Floor/building RAs facilitate community expectations and review university standards |

RCDs create their residential community presentation using the supplied agenda. Locations are communicated during fall training. The source separately links first-year and upper-division opening agendas, a Community Standards and Living Agreement Facilitation Guide, and a fillable standards document. Suite living agreements are in the suites housing portal.

## Winter transition

At the end of fall, floor/building RAs explain how residents should prepare their rooms for winter break, using the transition agenda.

## Spring opening

During the first spring week, floor/building RAs provide semester updates, introduce new residents to the community, and share housing-selection information. The agenda is provided during winter training.

## Spring closing

End-of-semester meetings explain checkout preparation. Follow the current closing agenda and supervisor instructions. This repository does not invent exact meeting dates or requirements absent from the source.

title: Policy and procedure document finder
content:
## Finding the applicable guidance

The policy page groups reference documents under Incident Protocols, Lockout Protocols, Maintenance Issues, and Conflict Mediation. The document catalog lists the titles observed in those groups.

## Incident references

The inventory covers medical and emotional crises, fire and evacuation, severe weather, building or utility failures, unwanted guests, violence and misconduct, substance-related incidents, missing students, pests and environmental concerns, and other community issues. These are generic reference titles, not records about individual incidents or residents.

## Other categories

- Lockout: hard-key checkout, Keytrak, Homebase, Northside on/off-campus, and South 40 swipe-door reference documents.
- Maintenance: filing maintenance and housekeeping requests.
- Conflict mediation: roommate agreements and a mediation presentation.

The page also links AED, emergency-bag, and incident-report resources. This collection provides source routing only for access controls and emergency details. Consult the current official documents and supervising staff; no emergency, medical, legal, or building-entry procedure is reconstructed from titles.
